title: Go testing
summary: Design table-driven Go tests that pin behavior, failure paths and cancellation, and run them only through the approved targeted verifier.

provenance.notes: Limited to flags the runtime verifier allow-lists: -run, -count, -v, -race and -timeout, with relative package paths.

inputs.name: behavior
inputs.description: The behavior under test, as input and expected output.

inputs.name: package
inputs.description: The package whose tests are in scope.

outputs.name: tests
outputs.description: Table-driven tests covering success, boundary and failure cases.

outputs.name: evidence
outputs.description: The verifier command and its exit status.

workflow.step: Write the table first: name, input, expected output or error, covering the happy path, each boundary and each documented failure.
workflow.check: Every row has a descriptive name.

workflow.step: Run each row with t.Run so a failure names the row; avoid shared mutable state between rows.
workflow.check: Rows can run in any order.

workflow.step: Assert on behavior and error values (errors.Is / errors.As), not on formatted strings, unless the string is the contract.
workflow.check: Renaming an internal helper does not break a test.

workflow.step: For concurrency and cancellation, use a cancelled context and a bounded wait; run with -race when the verifier allows it.
workflow.check: The test fails if the cancellation check is removed.

workflow.step: Confirm the new test fails against the old behavior, then passes against the new, using the targeted package only.
workflow.check: A test that never failed proves nothing.

constraints: Do not modify an existing test to make it pass; a failing existing test is a finding.
Use only the approved verifier: go test with allow-listed flags and a relative package path.
Tests must not touch the network, wall-clock sleeps longer than a second, or paths outside the repository.

examples.title: Boundary table
examples.guidance: Rows for 0, 1, 100 and 101 plus a non-numeric input, each asserting the exact error value.

verification: The targeted go test exits 0 and the new rows fail against a reverted change.
No existing test file was edited.
